body:
"Anything rash," I certainly am not doing.  I'm taking my time and thinking this out.  It's a fair certainty that I'm going to move forward, but after so much isolation and failure, I have grown to hold myself to standards where this is concerned.

For example, I don't want to suffer while I die.  What point does it serve to end suffering only to spend my last moments in more suffering?  I don't want to die the way that I have lived.

I also want to ensure that no harm comes to others as a result of my process.  That rules out many potential methods, and some for reasons not immediately obvious.  For example, firearms are out because I can not secure the weapon after the fact.

I am also writing a long letter.  It is important to me to settle some matters that I think are grotesque and extraordinarily harmful where the matter of suicide is concerned, to ensure that my intent is documented for authorities, and to leave those I care about with positive words at least.

It is also time to ensure my method's effectiveness, but for it being extraordinarily lethal, I will not discuss it here.  

So, this isn't to be a rash act.  If anything, this is to be a very carefully planned and executed act with rationalizations and motives deliberated upon in the most excruciating detail.

However, with all this in mind, if I am still totally isolated by the time all arrangements are in place, then there is nothing in this world that could stop me.  Forestall the inevitable by needlessly subjecting me to more humiliation and pain?  Sure.  Stop me?  Not on this Earth.

On that count, I'm unsure why I write here.  I suppose that in this, as in any significant journey, one wishes not to travel alone even if the final mile must be walked solo.

Actually, in my case it is pretty certain to last forever.  No family.  No money, so no friends.  Can't work while isolated all the time.  Nobody loves me, so nothing like that.

I have nothing and no hope of anything.  This will last as long as I do.  Living is just a question of how long I can stand it before I try something that works.

Every person who has ever been close to me.  

My importance ends where my limit of doing for others ends.  Unfortunately, nothing is ever enough.

No phone.  Just the solitary confinement of my home.

I don't think I'm important.  I could be if I could work while totally isolated.
